title: Still charged, so why is my phone battery already old?
description:
Little Q is taking pictures of squirrels in the park with Mom's old phone. It still has 20% charge, but the moment she taps to take a photo, the screen goes black. Is the phone broken? It still has charge, so how can the battery be old?

In this episode, the Chief and Little Q picture the battery as a water bottle that holds power: the percent is how full the bottle is right now, "Maximum Capacity" is how big the bottle itself still is, and how wide the spout is decides how fast power can pour out at once. A thin film, a lot like limescale, slowly grows inside the battery, shrinking the bottle and narrowing the spout. When the phone needs a big gulp of power and it can't pour out fast enough, the phone shuts itself off first to protect the parts inside.

We also talk about how phones look after their own batteries, why you can charge whenever you like, and why you should stop using a battery that is swollen or very hot and tell an adult.

The bottle and the scale are our metaphor, not how a battery is really built; the illustrations in this episode were made with AI and are diagrams. Most numbers in the video are approximate figures from phone makers' explanations; "nearly three years" is our own rough math, and every phone and every battery is different. The source of every claim is listed in the references below.
